title: Stabilize export stamping and offset logic for backdated quota credits
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Incidents over the past quarter show occasional invoice inaccuracies when backdated quota credits (rate limit or trial credits applied retroactively) are merged into Stripe/NetSuite exports. Root causes: non-deterministic export stamp assignment, late-arriving credit events not quarantined, and offset application that creates negative line items when applied to already-merged partial-hour lines. This ticket stabilizes export stamping and introduces a deterministic offsetting path for backdated credits to ensure invoice accuracy and idempotent exports.
acceptance_criteria: Export manifest includes monotonic export_stamp (epoch millis) and a seqnum per customer-day; manifests are idempotent and detect forks
Backdated credits are quarantined and produce a corrective export record rather than mutating historical invoice line timestamps
No negative line items produced in Stripe exports as a result of credit offsetting (simulated and verified in shadow export run)
End-to-end shadow export shows identical invoice totals after 7 days of synthetic late credit events
New export telemetry (Grafana) surfaces count of quarantined credits, corrective exports emitted, and seqnum forks
implementation_notes: Phase 1: Add export_stamp (millis) + per-customer sequence number computed from event ingestion watermark; persist in export_manifest table
Phase 2: Quarantine late credits arriving outside the export window and emit corrective export lines with tag corrective=true and original_effective_date preserved

Phase 3: Change offsetting logic to create a corrective negative adjustment line tied to a corrective export manifest instead of merging into historical invoice lines; ensure Stripe line_item dedupe keys include manifest.seqnum
Phase 4: Add shadow-run path: run new reconciler against a snapshot and compare Stripe/NetSuite output to baseline; fail build if invoice delta > $0.05 for >0.1% customers
Phase 5: Ship monitoring dashboards, alerts for seqnum fork rate > 0.01% and corrective exports > 0.5% of daily exports
Testing: unit tests for seqnum monotonicity, integration test using BigQuery replay harness, and canary shadow run against staging stripe sandbox
steps: Design schema migration for export_manifest (DB migration PR)
Implement stamp+seqnum assignment in exporter service (github PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/2897)
Implement quarantine queue and corrective export generator (github PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/2901)
Update Stripe export composer to include corrective=true metadata and manifest.seqnum in line_item.external_id
Create shadow-run job and backfill test data (BigQuery query: https://console.cloud.google.com/bigquery?p=prod&d=billing&t=shadow_test_query&page=1)
Add Grafana panels and alert rules (dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd1234/billing-exports)
Run staging shadow for 72h, validate diffs, and schedule rollout to canary customers
